headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: unstructured can write and network while awesome-python is non-runnable, making prompt-injection and leakage mostly blocked by the pair’s lack of a shared execution path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest unstructured’s outputs by default. unstructured can read/write files and use allowlisted network, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. This makes prompt injection via interaction pathway provably absent from the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF awesome-python is made runnable and parses unstructured output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe unstructured output into any instruction-following parser.
Require explicit human review before copying content between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and is non-runnable, while unstructured processes documents/images/text and can read/write files. A leakage path exists only if both are pointed at the same workspace or documents, and the blast radius is limited by the absence of secrets in profile A. No direct evidence shows shared storage or third-party exfiltration beyond allowlisted egress.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same document directory, leakage becomes plausible.
IF unstructured is given sensitive documents, its allowlisted egress should be reviewed before use.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive sample documents.
Disable network access for unstructured during review runs.
Check that no secrets are present in the shared workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no runtime write surface, but unstructured can write the filesystem, read files, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. If both are orchestrated over the same mutable directory, unstructured can overwrite artifacts or race with other processes. The conflict is not high because profile A lacks write capability, but the overlap is still real for shared outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF unstructured is run concurrently with another writer on shared outputs, race conditions may occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer per workspace.
Add a lock file around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where awesome-python produces authoritative facts that unstructured then acts on. awesome-python is a non-runnable collection, not an agent that generates operational outputs, and unstructured is a document processor rather than an action-taking controller. Without a verified handoff, cascading error is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator starts treating awesome-python entries as authoritative policy, reassess.
IF unstructured is wired to execute actions from parsed text, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep awesome-python as a reference-only catalog.
Require verification before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy conflict is documented for either profile. awesome-python touches no data and is non-runnable; unstructured lists documents/images/text but no regulated class such as PHI or EU PII. With only docs-only evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into unstructured, reassess compliance controls.
IF a residency or retention policy is later documented for either agent, re-evaluate the pair.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in test runs.
Review privacy policy links before production use.
